package_info.why_malicious: The application masquerades as a legitimate COVID-19 tracking app but contains ransomware functionality that locks the device by changing the password and displays a ransom note, denying user access until a ransom is paid.

execution_context.file_location: Covid19 Tracker Android APK (main activity code)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code forcefully changes the device's lock screen password and displays a ransom note overlay, denying user access to the device until a ransom is paid.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Changing the device password without user consent and displaying a ransom note is a classic ransomware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate COVID-19 tracking app should not alter device security settings or restrict user access.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Device management apps in enterprise settings may change passwords, but only with explicit user/admin consent.
key_indicators: Denial of user access to device

attack_chain.action: User is lured to a phishing site (coronavirusapp[.]site) and downloads the malicious APK.
User installs and launches the Covid19 Tracker app.
App executes code to change the device password and lock the screen.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is denied access to the device

attack_chain.action: App displays a ransom note demanding payment to unlock the device.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: extortion of ransom payment

behavioral_signatures: Android app changing device password without user interaction
Display of ransom note overlays after app launch
Denial of device access immediately after installation
file_indicators: APK files named Covid19 Tracker or similar
App requesting device admin privileges during installation
network_indicators: Distribution from coronavirusapp[.]site or similar COVID-19 themed phishing domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Android applications that request device admin privileges and attempt to change the device password immediately after installation, especially if distributed from unofficial sources or COVID-19 themed domains. Look for overlays displaying ransom notes and sudden loss of device access following installation of new apps.
